t:
Isle of Far-Far-Away? Of course, I visited it... It's a nice place, I'll say! Calmness, smoothness and goodness of Tenses.
A long time ago, when the world was not broken apart, there was one remote region, the name of which had not yet made its way into public records, and it was jokingly nicknamed the Kingdom of Far-Far-Away. It was pure wilderness; neither a horse rider nor a sure-footed person could pass through it. Forest for hundreds of miles! A wise keeper and a resurrected forest spirit ruled it. Those who dared visit the forest with wicked thoughts never returned, while the kind-hearted were shown the path.
After the Cataclysm, only a small piece remained of that forest, but it withstood time and did not melt away in the Astral. It was said that the keeper survived as well. I myself never saw her, but people say that her magic still protects the Isle of Far-Far-Away. Every traveler may look for rest and respite under the foliage of old trees. But Light help you if you enrage the forest mistress! They say she cannot stand it when someone brings harm to her protected animals!

Metalville... A vivid example of what can happen to soldiers when they have a lot of free time that is not employed with drill training or reading manuals.
This story was related to me by someone directly involved in the events, one of the few lucky ones that managed to escape the city that became a theater of war. Ten years ago Metalville was a small mining town populated by workers, and later, when the mine dried up, it was filled in and the city was handed over to the Imperial army as a training ground. To practice shooting, assaults and combat in an urban environment. In short, they organized teaching there. Blues against Reds, just like in the Igsh Military District, only the warriors trained there were serious, veterans, and their lessons were as close to reality as possible. Everything went strictly according to plan until a Blue General, a big Orc by the name of Gire the Merciless quarreled in front of all his officers with a Red General, Mountain Steel. The generals insulted each other, then parted. The Red one forgot about the argument, but the Blue one was so offended that he got his squadron up in the middle of the night and led them in an attack on the Reds. And this was no training attack, but a real one, with live ammunition. He had decided to wash away the insult with blood.
Darn it all if the soldiers didn't lose all touch with reality! The Blues made mincemeat of most of the Reds under cover of darkness, and as soon as it was light they realized that they would be facing a military tribunal, and be shot in a row up against the brick wall. Anyway, Gire and his loyal comrade Ryakha realized that they had nothing to lose, and they decided, with typical Orc stubbornness, to see things through to the end. Gire declared himself a great leader, and the Orcs - a superior race, and all others where but dust under their feet, and he planned to build a great Empire. Only they were unlucky - the astral ships managed to get out of Metalville. So the newly declared leaders of the Empire are now stuck in the besieged town, fighting with the remaining Reds and dreaming of a new Orc empire, under the leadership of the great and wise Gire. That's the much vaunted imperial discipline for you!

I've been to this allod. It really is a cemetery, and it is peaceful, indeed. It's old Kanial burial grounds that look gloomy and sad, with dark trees hanging over swampy hollows, and mossy gravestones, and mysterious shadows and lights in the depths. I chose not to land there, just in case. You shouldn't trouble the dead, or they will trouble you!

The Workshop? Of course, I've heard about it. Damn that place!

Alright, listen. Once upon a time this allod was a place where sorcerers gathered to do peaceful studies. You know, they had libraries, quiet cells, and lived in harmony with nature. The best place to practice, they said. How could we know that still waters ran deep? Eventually, we found out that they were experimenting with Sparks. They trapped them and transferred them to different bodies.

Our Defenders got rattled and tried to teach those experimentalists a lesson. That was a foolish thing to do... As soon as the sorcerers realized they were disclosed, they attacked. Few of our soldiers survived. The lucky survivors say that they confronted an army of wooden soldiers and golems. That is why the sorcerers started their experiments in the first place. To create a wooden army.

Oh, that's a nasty place. I remember telling my kids stories about beautiful and terrifying sirens who lured poor sailors with their enchanting songs. Who knew those stories were going to come true?

Astralonauts say that the whole place in overwhelmed with shipwrecks. When they flied by, they locked all the crew in the hold. Only the toughest stayed on the deck. The navigator even plugged his ears with wax to avoid temptation. They say, the song is really beautiful. So beautiful it makes you want to jump off the ship.

It is madness, for sure. This is why we have to end it. Be careful if you fly that way. The sailors said they saw the undead and strangely looking Elves on the isle. That must be Elven women who sing the songs!

Hm... I heard of a small allod, lost deep in the Astral. I've never been there actually. They say sinister things about it. Ships get lost... One friend of mine told me that when a ship approaches that island, its devices start to hiccup and the reactor boils!

And there's more. Once I met a drunken orc who claimed that once he was a cook on an Imperial trading ship, which crashed at that very allod. He spoke of the undead, of savages that eat humans, and of an ugly idol... Honestly, I didn't pay much attention to his drunken gibberish, but if you ever moor your ship to that allod, don't let go of your weapon!

Ah, Aoidoi. Their nation might be young, but their cities are impressive! New Bay is being constructed right now, but you can already tell it's going to be magnificent. Those stoneheads are brave, I'll give them that. This sector is swarming with crazy demons. I hope nothing evil will come of it.

I've heard that some demons don't want to fight and offer their friendship instead! I don't believe that. If the Aoidoi trust demons, they are more gullible than children.

We’re still not done with the damned Architects. Their main invasion was repelled, but they still dissipated across the whole world. A friend of mine told me that he sailed past an allod which once used to be green, and now its all stone. And they are there. Staring with their dead blue eyes. Ugh.

They must have reshaped the whole allod. Somebody’s got to get rid of them.
You want to know more? That's good. Well, ask, I'll gladly tell you what I know.

At the dawn of astral navigation, before the invention of visors when the first ships had to literally feel their way through, lighthouses were built on all the discovered islands. The light coming from a lighthouse could be seen from great distances and signaled, "Sail here, it's safe." Many a sailor who had lost their way in the astral counted their blessings having caught the glow of a lighthouse in the distance.
But as astral navigation developed, lighthouses lost their significance. With a modern visor, an astrolabe and a navigator, getting lost in the astral is virtually impossible. So these days lighthouses remain mostly as a tribute to the old ways, a place to rest, spend the night and shoot the breeze.
But recently I received dire news: an astral pirate gang seized one of the old lighthouses and turned it into a trap. As soon as a ship following its light docks, the gang boards the vessel, plunders and demolishes it, while its crew are forced to walk the plank into the astral!
What brutes! Barbarians! So many innocent people got hurt because of them. They must be stopped at any cost! And if you find any treasures, I'm sure the dead owners won't mind if you keep them...

Cold and more cold - that's all I can tell you about Kyoltmark. I haven't been there myself, but I know that one of the first gibberling ships once got shipwrecked on that icy rock. When League ships discovered it a few years later, the surviving gibberlings had already settled on that tiny piece of land, made themselves a cozy new home and flatly refused to leave.
But something bad happened not long ago: the island was attacked by astral demons. What's strange is that they didn't kill the inhabitants, but captured them instead. A mighty demon named Thought Catcher is said to have turned all the gibberlings into his slaves, who now serve him faithfully. What a terrible fate!
If you happen to visit this island, you will inevitably have to fight the insane gibberlings. Kill them without mercy, for the locals are now mere shells of themselves and under total control of demons!

I don't know much about that island. I heard that there's a high mountain at the center whose top is always white with snow. And that it's home to a tribe of wild goblins. And I'm not talking about servants of the Empire type goblins either; no, these are authentically wild - with stone spears and clubs for weapons and all. People say they're a real angry bunch!
Some ten years ago the Empire tried to subdue the native goblins and drive them into the mines, but they failed! Someone stepped up that the goblins essentially deified, and inspired them to put up such a fierce resistance that the Imperial soldiers retreated. And I bet plenty of breeches were soiled in the process, he-he.
As far as I understand, this creature is not a god so much as a powerful spellcaster. Eyewitness reports suggest that he's not human, not an elf, and not even arisen! Though I can't imagine who else but the dragons themselves could repel a whole squad of Imperial Punishers. The point is you had best watch your back. False gods always surround themselves with insane fanatics, ready to lie on the altar or sacrifice their lives in battle at the whim of their false god.

Scoundrels! All of them at the Clear Mountain are scoundrels and murderers! They've killed countless innocent people. And what for?! Because they don't believe in Light, you see!
That place used to be an ordinary village where decent villagefolk lived, paid their taxes on time and respected their nobles - life was it should be. No one harassed, oppressed or smothered them with taxes. Would else could simple folk want from life?
But as soon as that damned magus Jaromir showed up out of nowhere, preaching his filth about people betraying the faith of their ancestors and worshipping a false idol... How dare he call Tensess a "false idol"?! If it weren't for him, none of us would even be alive!
The magus totally scrambled the villagers' brains! They broke away from the League, tossed all the discontented into the astral, and are now worshiping spirits and elements, offering them sacrifices and oblations. Should a stranger come to their island, he's as good as dead!
Man, what I wouldn't give to toss Jaromir himself into the astral... But he has three loyal defenders at his side at all times: Alexei, Ivan and Vlad, all three exceptionally strong. Brainwashed by the magus, they'll rip anyone apart to defend their new ancestral faith. These defenders are like babies - all their power is in their muscles, not in their brains. So, if you decide to challenge Jaromir, remember that the whole village will come to his aid!

So you want to become a Historian, do you? I'm not surprised. Any researcher would give their right arm without a second thought for the chance to examine Koch Itzmahl.
Just imagine: a fully preserved temple from the golden age of the June Empire. Not the same wretched ruins you see everywhere, but a whole complex of temples.
Truth be told, I caught but a glimpse of it and almost fell overboard from shock! Bas-reliefs, frescos, statues, carved pillars... Just think how many secrets it conceals, not to mention treasures... Only there's no way to reach them!
Lizards have overrun the whole island. Before we could even land they showered us with javelins, hurled a huge fireball that tore a hole in our sail, and vowed to rip out our hearts and lay them on their ancestral altar if they ever saw us again. Their leader Shisskh was especially raging. What vicious creatures they are! We had to turn around fast and leave empty-handed.
Cleansing the temple of the lizards would be a noble endeavor that serves the Light... Not to mention incredibly profitable!

Thanks to heroes who are not afraid to go boldly forth and, with a steady hand, guide their astral ships to the deepest layers, it has been possible to learn a lot about the properties of the astral. For example, in the deepest layers there are islands about which nobody had heard before! If you want, I will tell you about them.
What is it you would like to know about?

Astral reflections occur only in the deepest layers of the Astral. On the outside, they look like real and familiar locations, but their content differs greatly from what you would expect. For example, a castle where some knight used to live will be occupied by undead or werewolves in its reflection. Where a river used to run, lava or corrosive acid may flow. Enemies may not appear as what they seem...
As I understand, astral reflections are images of the future, past or present that reveal a possible outcome of an event. Exploring these reflections is very dangerous, since you can never know what you will deal with, but the reward upon a victory may be significant!

Greetings!

I've been to the Astral far and wide. And I'm still up for more travels! I'll gladly share my knowledge with you.

I assume you already know that Imperial research in the fields of magic and science is performed in top secret labs.
However, the glorious history of our progress has one dark spot. I am talking about the Lab 9.
Yasskul Skritam, Tep cultist who follows his Master will zealously, has interfered into our experiments and revived the Plague, ancient disease that exterminated the Zem people.
Now the island is in total control of the diseased. There is no possibility to cure them. We can only bring peace to both these people and General Novikov, the head of the Lab 9 now known as Plague General. You also should get rid of infected zombies carrying the disease. And of course you should kill Yasskul Skitram who caused all troubles at the plagued island.
Can you handle it?

Have you ever been to the Vortex Isle?

An icy rock hovering in the Astral. A tomb of the Great Dragon defeated back in June times can be found there. Dragon's ghost has been guarding the Tomb for thousands of years.

There is an abundant supply of meteorite ore on the isle, so we are extremely interested in getting control over it. Perhaps you can help?

Listen carefully. In order to get to the Wraith, you will have to fight Glacier Elementals, Wild Yetis in the cave and Harpies that guard the pass to the Great Dragon's Tomb. Only near the Tomb you will be able to see the Wraith and defeat it.

During my travels I try to keep away from Wolf Island. There is an old legend about this death trap, a Kanian village that became a feeding ground for a werewolf.

A long, long time ago Kanian druid Vseslav the Charming got so close with the wolves from the island that he learned how to transform into one. He became their leader, and his neighbors were his first victims. After a while the whole island became infested with wolves and werewolves. Unlucky travelers who ventured to the island were eaten by predators.

If you want to perform a feat, Wolf island is just the place for it. Here's my advice: think twice before you challenge the pack!

In one of the expeditions I discovered an Astral isle that must have fallen apart from Holy Land. There is a Site of Power on this isle, a rich source of the Holy magic for which both League and Empire would die for.

The trouble is that the local folks have created a cult of blood around it. They are sure that the Gift of Resurrection had been brought to them by the Scorpion King, a giant creature that they call Serket. Both Waterfolks and Forestfolks strive for his grace fighting each other. They sacrifice living creatures to be devoured alive, and these poor victims can never be resurrected. But the people of this isle believe that these sacrifices ensure resurrection to the others.

This amok has to be stopped. It dishonors the idea of the Light. The Empire needs to take this Site of Power under its control! However, the waterfolks and the forestfolks are not going to have you challenge their poisonous king. You will have to fight them first. The waterfolks are the strongest, so they are going to be your primary target.

But your ultimate foe is Serket, the Scorpion King.

Have you heard the legend of the Isle of the Damned? This sad story proves that one evil soul can be worse than the whole world of evil.

Once upon a time there was a small village on some distant Astral island. Nice and honest people lived there. A loving couple was among them - Ivan and Maria, who got married and lived happily.....for a while. It should have been the perfect end of their fairy tale... but it wasn't.

A foreigner lived in that village. He was not a good one, but a man with a greedy and envious soul. He craved Maria's beauty and tried to approach her, but Maria brushed him off.

When Ivan and Maria got married he was out if his mind and decided to ruin their lives. He stole Maria's wedding ring, Ivan's love letter and a bunch of wedding flowers. He used these items to cast an evil curse on the young couple.

They went off to their graves soon and were buried together. But evil does not just vanish - an awful curse fell on the whole island and the villain himself. He died and turned into an undead.

You must find the wedding ring, the letter and the flowers, bring them to the grave and free the poor souls.

I'd never recommend you to mess with Draconids. They are dangerous. Even Demon Hunters who forged an alliance with them don't trust them completely. Why? Because Draconids don't share their secrets to anyone! Even to their friends.

I don't know what they are hiding in their Green Maze. Historians who explored it couldn't get to its depths, the way was blocked with a magic barrier. Once they tried to get through it, two High Draconids, Border Guards as they called themselves, appeared to drive the Historians away. From that day, Draconids would always meet unwelcomed guests with steel.

If you are willing to take a risk, try to solve the mystery of the Green Maze. However, you must find the path into the ancient ruins yourself.

The Silent Hills... I used to visit them quite often. I talked to ordinary Kanian people without fear, enjoyed their delicious fresh bread. Oh what a blessed land... it was.

Now this Isle is haunted. The ghosts live lives like normal people - they fish, hunt, grind flour. But when I arrived there the last time, they were not happy to see me or my crew. We barely escaped!

I'm puzzled! What kind of evil came to Silent Hills? Who cursed these people?

If you're brave enough to challenge this mystery, follow my advice. Search the Dark Forest! This had always been a nasty place. Maybe the evil that had been sleeping there woke up! Your way there will certainly be full of danger.

Remember that you will have to fight the ghosts to cleanse the Isle. This is the pain you will have to overcome. Keep in mind that you're giving them freedom, not death.

My friend Roman Kuzin, traveler and researcher, was unlucky to get stranded on the Lost Isle. I haven't heard from him since then...

The Lost Isle has its legend. This is the legend of Tep's Pyramid that came into its own mind and started raising the undead. People say that the one who manages to conquer the Pyramid, will receive a great treasure.

Roman was dreaming of this adventure. He learned a lot about this island. I will tell you everything I know if you agree to save my friend.

On the Lost Isle you will face Magic Elementals that are spawned by the powers of the Pyramid. You will also come across a lot of undead. Destroy them to get to the Pyramid and find a way to disable it, and you will be rewarded.

So? Will you help me?

What do you know about Goblins?

On the one hand, they are just miserable creatures. Everybody makes fun of them and despises them. There are all sorts of goblin jokes, and they are also known as pets for orc shamans. Sometimes I feel pity for them.

And on the other hand, they are thieves and bandits. Scoundrels, they are always up to something evil! Have you ever met goblin weapon dealers in Coba Plateau? Then you know what I am talking about!

Goblins have their own island in the Astral. This is their citadel, their republic! They even elect a... there's one funny word for it... a President! For the third time in a row they re-elect a shaman named Urub. It's he who's responsible for goblin raids on our allods.

If you happen to find this island, enforce the death sentence to the goblin "President"!

Have you ever heard of the Volcano Isle?

A Draconid tribe used to live on that island. They worshipped the God of Fire, who was sleeping in the crater of the dormant volcano. Sacrifices maintained his sleep and contained his rage.

But when the High Priest of the Draconids died, the knowledge of the ritual was buried with him. The volcano erupted and a powerful fire elemental escaped! He created four guards out of magma and flame - these huge manticores would turn anyone to ashes with their hot breath!

Many Draconids died, but the most cunning of them survived. They bring Crawler hearts in special bowls as sacrifices to protect themselves from fire.

If you ever try to drive the elementals back into the volcano, remember: do not attempt to attack the elemental while the manticores are alive! The God of Fire distributed his power among them, so killing the guards will make him weaker.

That's all I know. Good luck!

During one of my expeditions I was unlucky enough to visit the Tomb Isle. At first it appeared a silent and deserted place, a quiet home to one of Tep's Pyramids.

My second visit was proof of the terrible news of Tep's revived cult. Now his followers rule there. They use rock elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I don't know what they're looking for. They attacked me and my team, my people were badly wounded, so we had to leave the Isle really fast. I feel bad about it.

I'd like to ask you to find this Isle and put an end to the cultists.

I have never been to the Border Isle.

It is called like that because it often floats near Holy Land. It's not a surprise that both League and Empire fought for this allod to use it as a basecamp and to fortify their positions. We lucky enough to capture it first.

Anyway, access to the Isle is denied now. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Border Isle has betrayed the Empire! Obviously, demons cultists appeared among the soldiers. Or it may as well have happened because of the Astral worm entrenched in the middle of the Isle... They say it's able to corrupt people's minds.

Elizaveta Rysina herself has recently asked me about heroes willing to help the Empire. At the moment our army cannot afford sending an expedition to the Isle, but someone has to punish the traitors!

Maybe you have already encountered creatures corrupted by the Astral. It transforms them, usually for the worse...

Astral Horn is one of these creatures. It's a unicorn that was turned into a dangerous monster. It's not easy to find and very difficult to defeat. But I know a thing that might be helpful...

When you find the Astral Horn Isle, you will have to smash your way through the Astral crystals using the Hammer of Pain. You will get it by defeating Splasher, a fierce water elemental. You will also have to fight against Granite Trolls to find Shards of Pain. Power concealed in them can be used to charge your weapon with magic in the June Ruins guarded by a cyclops called Stomper.

With the charged Hammer, you will be able to break through the magic defenses blocking the way to Horn's den.

I'm not sure what you will find there. Be prepared to anything. I know that Astral Horn is hard to find. It's a master of camouflage.

Good luck!

Oh, you heard the rumors about this island?

A mysterious place. It's an ancient June Forge captured by Tep's cultists. Nobody knows what is happening there. I heard of a group of reckless travelers who dared to enter the depths of the ancient volcano where the Forge is located.

Only one of them came back. He said that cultists are trying to take control over ancient June machines, trying to turn them into their loyal servants. If they succeed...

The June's genius combined with Tep's insanity... Ouch... Be extremely careful if you are up to this adventure.

Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace? You wouldn't believe me, but there is such a place! It's called Enoch Island.

It was once a real backwater, with just two towns. Not so long ago some vampires forsook their creator, Armando de Doucer, and arrived on the island. They somehow came to an agreement with the peasants, bartering their own goods, healing magic and other useful things for blood. Everything has changed when the werewolves got to Enoch.

A vicious pack of half-wit beasts came barging in, bringing an end to the peace that the island had once enjoyed. Their chief, Luth the Meager, a former ringleader of a gang of thieves, vowed to devour anyone who failed to bow before him. The vampires protected themselves from the werewolves with a magic barrier, and closed the roads between the villages. Alongside the peasants, they have been resisting the monsters' attacks, but their strength is fading.

So if your travels happen to take you to Enoch Island, be prepared for quite a fight! Before getting at their leader, you will have to cleanse both villages of werewolves.

Yes, I've heard of that town. White-17 is a top secret military settlement, hidden deep in the Astral. As far as I know, there is something to hide! You see, Imperial scientists in White-17 were engaged in extremely dangerous research. People say that lead researcher Nomarkh Ebol maintained close relationship with Yasskul Setnakhte. Well, I've already told you about Setnakhte and the incident at the Lab Nine.
We have lost touch with White-17 a short time ago. I'm afraid they got into trouble just like General Novikov and his subordinates. So if you happen to come across the snow-covered isle guarded by Imperial soldiers, I'd suggest you to sail away. But should you decide to land, find Valentine Shtammin, a friend of mine and chief engineer there. He is smart, reliable and always ready to help. I have a feeling there is something wrong with White-17...

Once a circus with merry clowns and acrobats, this place did not enjoy much popularity recently. Who would fly through the dangers of the Astral to see a performance? No wonder the isle has come to rack and ruin.

All of a sudden, three guys appeared, who called themselves "masters of dreams". They repaired the old circus building and sent out invitations to a carnival. They promise that their incredible show will fulfill people's long-time dreams and desires.

As for me, I think they are charlatans. They don't want money at all, this is very strange. Be on your guard, it can be a trap!

So, are you one of those interested in these events?

It was once an Imperial mine, where hundreds of goblins were gathering precious strategic resources under watchful eyes and loud swearing of our foremen. There were also natives - kobolds and mountainfolks, but they were granted a status of honorary Imperial citizens by a special decree number... what was it... 123/16, I guess... So they were obliged to work for the welfare of their new motherland.

But those scums didn't want to work! They had no idea of discipline! These lazybones didn't believe in our bright future.

They conspired with a smart goblin, Gym the Cheapskate. Trolls also joined their side, and together they managed to drive away our foremen and engineers! Now they are living as a commune under the leadership of Gym. He ordered to block all tunnels, so they think they are safe.

But every day is not Sunday! There is a group of goblin demolishers on this isle who are still loyal to the Empire. They can break through the rock to the den of separatists and plunderers.

You are allowed to punish Gym and take all his belongings. The Empire will honor you!

Is that a serious question? Man, I'd give anything to forget that island, but I can't...
A long time ago, Kanian druids took a sprout of the Great Tree to a small desert island and transformed its lifeless rocks into a veritable paradise. I was lucky enough to have been there and I can honestly attest that even in our beloved Empire you won't find many places that could compare to the former glory of that beautiful sunny island. The local pagans had wise mentor named Dobroslav Radov - a truly cordial host who welcomed me, an Imperial servant, with open arms, paying no mind to politics! As he bid me farewell at the end of my visit, I departed with plentiful warm memories of the birds singing, crystal clear lakes, delicious birch sap and rustling leaves.
But recently I came to hear dire news. One night a giant spider, spawned by the astral, made its way to the Great Tree and poisoned it, causing Dobroslav and all his followers to go mad. He now calls himself Evildoer the Poisonous, and there's nothing left in him of the kind-hearted sage he used to be. Instead, he and his servants offer bloody sacrifices to the Desecrated Tree! The entire island swarms with venomous spiders that their queen, the Black Widow, breeds at a frightening pace. Blackvenom is hiding somewhere in the heart of the forest... But if one were to tear out the hearts of the insane pagans and burn them in the cleansing fire, thereby giving them peace, Blackvenom is sure to show himself. And if he dies, the corruption shall be gone from the forest forever.
I beg you to cleanse the Desecrated Forest! Kill the Widow and Blackvenom, and maybe the soul of he who was once Dobroslav will find peace...

Cold and more cold - that's all I can tell you about Kyoltmark. I haven't been there myself, but I know that one of the first gibberling ships once got shipwrecked on that icy rock. When League ships discovered it a few years later, the surviving gibberlings had already settled on that tiny piece of land, made themselves a cozy new home and flatly refused to leave.
But something bad happened not long ago: the island was attacked by astral demons. What's strange is that they didn't kill the inhabitants, but captured them instead. A mighty demon named Thought Catcher is said to have turned all the gibberlings into his slaves, who now serve him faithfully. What a terrible fate! If you happen to visit this island, you will inevitably have to fight the insane gibberlings. Kill them without mercy, for the locals are now mere shells of themselves and under total control of demons!

Oh yeah, I know that island. Once I visited it on a missionary mission. You see, there's a tribe of genuinely wild goblins living at the White Mountain. Those poor bastards don't even know about the Great Nezeb! They are completely ignorant and aggressive to boot! They wanted to sacrifice our missionaries to some scaly beast, whom the locals actually believe to be a god! Sacrilege!
After the missionaries departed from the island, the Committee dispatched a squad of Punishers to teach those dirty pagans the basics of the true faith, mutual respect and worship of the Trinity Church.
I don't know what happened on the island, but I do know that the squad soon returned from the island all roughed up and pissed off like you wouldn't believe. Following this incident the island's coordinates and the data on the two Imperial expeditions to the White Mountain were classified.
However, I did hear rumors and gossip about some idol that the local hairy wildlings worship. Supposedly it was he that gave his servants the strength to repel seasoned Imperial fighters.
If you do end up traveling to the White Mountain, remember that those fanatics won't listen to reason. Brute force is the only reason they'll understand!

I know that place. Only I don't recommend going there!
There's a whole village of religious fanatics on that island. Filthy peasants who grew turnips for Kanian soldiers only yesterday suddenly got too big for their breeches. They rejected the Light, to say nothing of saints like Nezeb and Skrakan, and now began worshiping some elements instead. They're led by a magus called Jaromir. It was that bearded psycho that incited a revolt among the peasantry! He completely brainwashed the villagefolk with stories about their ancestors' faith, the greatness of ancient Kania and its glorious traditions... Sure, traditions are sacred, no question about it. But you can't just throw reason out the window! I mean, we're building mana stations and subways, the League is breathing down our necks with their own industry, and they're still a thousand years behind. Well, what can you do? They're a dark, ignorant people, nothing like the enlightened citizens of our great Empire.
Anyway, should your path take you to the Clear Mountain, be prepared to fight the whole damn village. They have also got local heroes named Alexei, Ivan and Vlad - massive goons who will beat the daylights out of anyone if you give them cause. But if you manage to defeat Jaromir, perhaps the peasants will wise up and quit tossing visitors into the astral...

So you want to become a Historian, do you? I'm not surprised. Any researcher would give their right arm without a second thought for the chance to examine Koch Itzmahl.
Just imagine: a fully preserved temple from the golden age of the June Empire. Not the same wretched ruins you see everywhere, but a whole complex of temples.
Truth be told, I caught but a glimpse of it and almost fell overboard from shock! Bas-reliefs, frescos, statues, carved pillars... Just think how many secrets it conceals, not to mention treasures... Only there's no way to reach them!
Lizards have overrun the whole island. Before we could even land they showered us with javelins, hurled a huge fireball that tore a hole in our sail, and vowed to rip out our hearts and lay them on their ancestral altar if they ever saw us again. Their leader Shisskh was especially raging. What vicious creatures they are! We had to turn around fast and leave empty-handed.
Cleansing the temple of the lizards would be a noble endeavor that serves the Light... Not to mention incredibly profitable!

Are you seriously asking me this question? Rotswamp is the filthiest place in the entire astral. The soil sloshes underfoot, moisture seeps under your clothes, there are heaps of dirt swarming with insects and the fog is so thick you can't even see your own feet. To make a long story short, you won't find a nastiest place to visit than Rotswamp! Countless travelers have gone there and never come back... And no wonder, with deadly creatures lurking at every corner!
When I had the ill luck of joining an expedition to that filthy swamp, we lost three guards to hydras on the very first day. They are terrible venom-spitting creatures. We dubbed the oldest of them Echidna after it tore a pack horse in two with a single bite!
One night we awoke to horrible screaming: our camp was attacked by Lamias. Armed to their teeth, they killed our sentry and charged right at us, screaming something about two sisters craving our blood. We barely managed to fight them off!
However, in our retreat we passed through the center of the swamp, where the greatest danger of all awaited us. We had scarcely enough time to wonder why the Lamias suddenly stopped their pursuit when a gigantic drake swooped down on our group out of the night sky, spitting fire all around. Smaller drakes circled above our heads to make sure no one would escape. Miraculously, I managed to survive by falling into the mud and digging in so that the drakes couldn't see me. My companions weren't so lucky...
Come morning, when the drakes finished their bloody feast and flew away, I slinked my way back to the ship. Exhausted, wounded and covered in mud from head to toe, I nearly burst into tears when I saw the ship waiting for us. Right then and there I swore that I'd never set foot in that cursed place again!

Why are you so interested in Zone 51, anyway? You shouldn't even know the name, Zone 51. This information is classified, if you didn't know!
Then again, seeing as you were directly involved in the events in Lab 13, I think you have a right to know the truth about the Empire's secret military base in the Kanian Archipelagos. Listen carefully, and remember - this stays between us!
Zone 51 is a military laboratory that continued to conduct research and experimenting with mental influence on mass consciousness after the Lab 13 incident. Project manager Nomarkh Sadaffee decided to fuse together psionic influence and physical modification of the body. In his view, the imperfect human system is incapable of manipulating its own consciousness to the fullest extent, let alone influence others. Therefore, he decided to combine prosthetic technologies of the Arisen with the subjects' psionic abilities. The resulting war machines, controlled by the power of thought, could have become the perfect army - untiring, resource-independent, incapable of betrayal... But it was Nomarkh Sadaffee himself who turned traitor! The latest info suggests that he's managed to destroy or subdue the entire Zone 51 security team. There's been no communication with the military base, and no one knows what's going on there.
So remember, if you see a lovely tropical isle in the Astral with dark metal hangars jutting out over the emerald jungle, landing on it could end up being the biggest mistake of your life... And quite possibly, the last!

Just a minute, I will look in my notes. Hmm... Aha, there it is! A note on the addition to the astral charts of a new island, on which old June ruins were discovered. Well, well...
In short, I know almost nothing about this island. It doesn't even have a name! According to our scouts, a Kanian exploration ship discovered an island in the depths of the astral, on which June ruins have been preserved since the time of the June civilization. As the ruins are of enormous scientific value, the League quickly sent a ship to the island bearing an archaeological expedition under the command of one Lisa Livingrock. The expedition reached the island and started to dig, after which all contact with them was lost. Their last message said that the scientists had almost reached the entrance to the central crypt of the June tomb. They also complained about Kobalds, which had appeared from who knows where.
Right now nothing is known about the fate of the expedition. If you want to know my opinion - the scientists dug up something they shouldn't have dug up. The thirst for knowledge, just like the thirst for profit, leads to nothing good.

The Black Rock... You will recognize it immediately when you approach the island! A lifeless piece of bare rock, gouged by demonic fangs. It is teeming with demons there!
As far as I know, the Black Rock is all that was left of the de Blizare House allod after the Night of Astral Portals.
The de Blizare House suffered enormous losses that night. Almost all their mages died in combat, the Great Mage lost heart and prepared to open a portal to Kania, which fatally undermined the morale of the defenders. The elves ran off, leaving their allod to be destroyed by the demons. However, for some reason unknown to me, the allod was extremely resistant to the impact of the astral. They say that this was due to the blood of the elven martyrs, who defended their abode to the last... But I don't believe that! Elves are mendacious and egotistical creatures, that are not given over to heroic self sacrifice. Although, by their standards such a death would probably be considered beautiful.
Anyway, right now the Black Rock is a piece of land teeming with demons. They are like fleas on a goblin there! So, I strongly advise you against even going near that island. An armada of demons is not something you would like to encounter in the astral.

The Underwater Kingdom? Nobody can say for sure whether it exists or not. I am not able to lie, so I will tell you what I know.
I heard this story from a Kanian merchant. His name was Granger, or Gardener or something like that. He was a rich merchant, he was friendly with the Free Traders, they say that he was planning an Oligarchy. He transported goods to and fro throughout the entire astral, he was always on the road. His wife, who had both brains and beauty, saw her husband every six months, if she was lucky. But she didn't complain.
One day it happened that Gardner's ship wandered off the caravan trail. He saw a small island, not even an island, more like a clod of land with a well and an abandoned hut. As luck would have it, the crew's water supplies were low. They dropped anchor, and Gardener went ashore to drink some water. He had barely bent over when a cold hand reached out of the well and grabbed him by the beard! And a dull voice echoed from under the water: "Promise to give me that which you have, but about which you know nothing, otherwise I will drown you!"
Gardener was scared, and he immediately promised to hand over that about which he knew nothing. If you don't know it, you won't miss it! The water spirit let him go, but as soon as the merchant reached home, he started to pull out his hair. His wife met him on the threshold with a young child. The merchant was horror struck - he had promised to give his own child to the water fiend!
But it's true when they say that merchants learn to count before they can read. Gardener remembered that he was last home more than a year ago, and he could see that the child was no more than a month old! The wife was unable to balance her debit and credit columns - the child was someone else's. Gardener threw out his wayward wife along with the child, and he gave his clerk, whom he had left in charge, a good beating - the child's features were suspiciously like those of the clerk. The merchant took to the drink something chronic, and drank away his fortune, down to the last copper. And he told the water spirit, when he came at his appointed time to collect his debt, that he could sing for it, and he paid him his interest in kicks and punches.
What a sad tale. If you see a small island with a well in the astral, don't think twice, throw a barrel of explosives down the well, to teach that water field who reduces honest people to poverty a lesson!

Cinderland... Now that little island has no other name. But at one time it was the best hunting reserve in the Empire. It is said that the Great Yasker himself loved to shoot ducks or deer in this reserve. The ranger there, Kuzmich, is a famous drinker - there were times when we drank so much that come morning we forgot which of us was the ranger and which the traveler. Hmm, those were the days... Now only charred stumps remain, with feral beasts roaming around. May that mad Arisen be cursed!
He was initially received as a welcome guest. And why not? A famous scientist decides to do some research in the quiet of the forest! They set up everything for him - a laboratory in the forest, all nice and quiet. He worked away, and the vials clinked... Then Kuzmich, kind soul that he is, decided to try and find a drinking companion. Well, I suppose he couldn't drink with the bears! He got into the habit of visiting the mage for a chat about science and a couple of bottles. And Kuzmich's booze is strong stuff! It was nothing to Kuzmich, he has a tin throat and steel liver, but the magician drank himself silly. And in a drunken fit he tore down his tower along with its foundations.
The scoundrel torched the forest! He imagined himself to be Fireborn, a Great Fire Mage, the lord of flame, damn him to hell. That was it, an end to the reserve - he really was a Great Mage, so the forest there keeps burning but never burns out, the beasts are burned but not roasted, and worst of all, the spirit of the forest, old Oakster, fell under his spell and is now in his service. Kuzmich went off the rails with grief, he doesn't recognize anybody, just drinks and drinks. I tired to reason with him, but he gave me a smack in the face and kicked me out of my hut, where there was a pack of fire wolves waiting for me. They chased me right back to my ship, and burned such a hole in my trousers, it's not funny! I was lucky I didn't have my skin burned off. So, if you are planning to visit Cinderland, which is all that is left of the reserve, don't forget to bring a fire extinguisher - believe me, the flames are still blazing away there like crazy.

Isle of Far-Far-Away? Of course, I visited it... It's a nice place, I'll say! Calmness, smoothness and goodness of Tenses.

A long time ago, when the world was not broken apart, there was one remote region, the name of which had not yet made its way into public records, and it was jokingly nicknamed the Kingdom of Far-Far-Away. It was pure wilderness; neither a horse rider nor a sure-footed person could pass through it. Forest for hundreds of miles! A wise keeper and a resurrected forest spirit ruled it. Those who dared visit the forest with wicked thoughts never returned, while the kind-hearted were shown the path.

After the Cataclysm, only a small piece remained of that forest, but it withstood time and did not melt away in the Astral. It was said that the keeper survived as well. I myself never saw her, but people say that her magic still protects the Isle of Far-Far-Away. Every traveler may look for rest and respite under the foliage of old trees. But Light help you if you enrage the forest mistress! They say she cannot stand it when someone brings harm to her protected animals!

Metalville... A vivid example of what can happen to soldiers when they have a lot of free time that is not employed with drill training or reading manuals.

Ten years ago Metalville was a small mining town populated by workers, and later, when the mine dried up, it was filled in and the city was handed over to the Imperial army as a training ground. To practice shooting, assaults and combat in an urban environment. In short, they organized teaching there. Blues against Reds, just like in the Igsh Military District, only the warriors trained there were serious, veterans, and their lessons were as close to reality as possible. Everything went strictly according to plan until a Blue General, a big Orc by the name of Gire the Merciless quarreled in front of all his officers with a Red General, Mountain Steel. The generals insulted each other, then parted. The Red one forgot about the argument, but the Blue one was so offended that he got his squadron up in the middle of the night and led them in an attack on the Reds. And this was no training attack, but a real one, with live ammunition. He had decided to wash away the insult with blood.

Darn it all if the soldiers didn't lose all touch with reality! The Blues made mincemeat of most of the Reds under cover of darkness, and as soon as it was light they realized that they would be facing a military tribunal, and be shot in a row up against the brick wall. Anyway, Gire and his loyal comrade Ryakha realized that they had nothing to lose, and they decided, with typical Orc stubbornness, to see things through to the end. Gire declared himself a great leader, and the Orcs - a superior race, and all others where but dust under their feet, and he planned to build a great Empire. Only they were unlucky - the astral ships managed to get out of Metalville. So the newly declared leaders of the Empire are now stuck in the besieged town, fighting with the remaining Reds and dreaming of a new Orc empire, under the leadership of the great and wise Gire, bad luck to him, the treacherous cur!

I've been to this allod. It really is a cemetery, and it is peaceful, indeed. It's old Kanial burial grounds that look gloomy and sad, with dark trees hanging over swampy hollows, and mossy gravestones, and mysterious shadows and lights in the depths. I chose not to land there, just in case. You shouldn't trouble the dead, or they will trouble you!

Workshop? Yes, I've heard about it... That's one wicked place, mark my words.

They say, all kinds of sorcerers used to gather there to practice in peace and quiet. But their practices have gone too far: they started experimenting on Sparks, trapping them and transferring them to different bodies. It's like a filial agency of Tep's Pyramid! Surely, both the League and the Empire were outraged by these experiments. But the sorcerers did not really care and just threw all the objectors to the Astral.

Some devilry has been going on on that isle ever since. Those who flied by say that the sorcerers had started cutting down trees and building wooden soldiers and golems. Just think of it! What if that army comes alive and attacks our allods? Messing with Sparks has done no one any good.

Have you ever heard legends about enchanting Sirens' songs and shipwrecks caused by them? Well, those legends are real.

One of the distant allods is occupied by an Elven tribe - I can find no other way to call those savages. Astralonauts report that music and singing can be heard coming from the Sirens' Rock, and it makes ship crews rush to their own destruction. It is difficult to resist that magic, but it is possible if there is a gifted specialist on board. Or a deaf thug.

The amount of ship wrecks speaks for itself. It's hard to imagine how many fair sailors have fallen prey to those bloodthirsty creatures! What has happened to them? Were they eaten alive? By the way, the undead were also seen on that Rock...

I strongly recommend you to avoid that isle. We should have sent there a squad of Mentalists long ago and destroyed that trash from a safe distance.

Hm... I heard of a small allod, lost deep in the Astral. I've never been there actually. They say sinister things about it. Ships get lost... One friend of mine told me that when a ship approaches that island, its devices start to hiccup and the reactor boils!

And there's more. Once I met a drunken orc who claimed that once he was a cook on an Imperial trading ship, which crashed at that very allod. He spoke of the undead, of savages that eat humans, and of an ugly idol... Honestly, I didn't pay much attention to his drunken gibberish, but if you ever moor your ship to that allod, don't let go of your weapon!

At the dawn of astral navigation, before the invention of visors, when the first ships had to literally feel their way through, lighthouses were built on all the discovered islands. The light coming from a lighthouse could be seen from great distances and signaled, "Sail here, it's safe."

But, as astral navigation developed, lighthouses lost a good deal of their importance. So these days lighthouses remain mostly as a tribute to the old ways, a place to rest, spend the night and shoot the breeze.

But recently I received dire news: an astral pirate gang seized one of the old lighthouses and turned it into a trap. As soon as a ship following its light docks, the gang boards the vessel, plunders and demolishes it, while its crew are forced to walk the plank into the astral!

What brutes! Barbarians! So many innocent people got hurt because of them. They must be stopped at any cost! And if you find any treasures, I'm sure the dead owners won't mind if you keep them...

Thanks to heroes who are not afraid to go boldly forth and, with a steady hand, guide their astral ships to the deepest layers, it has been possible to learn a lot about the properties of the astral. For example, in the deepest layers there are islands about which nobody had heard before! If you want, I will tell you about them.

Do you want to know more? That's good. Curiosity is not a vice, but an optimal way to get to know the world. If it weren't for my curiosity, how would I ever come to know so many interesting tidbits about the astral? I wouldn't know even a tenth of the wonders an adventurer could encounter on their journey!
Feel free to ask, I will tell you everything I know. If it's now about military secrets or any other classified information, of course.

Astral reflections occur only in the deepest layers of the Astral. On the outside, they look like real and familiar locations, but their content differs greatly from what you would expect. For example, a castle where some knight used to live will be occupied by undead or werewolves in its reflection. Where a river used to run, lava or corrosive acid may flow. Enemies may not appear as what they seem...
As I understand, astral reflections are images of the future, past or present that reveal a possible outcome of an event. Exploring these reflections is very dangerous, since you can never know what you will deal with, but the reward upon a victory may be significant!
There’s something wrong about this allod...
There’s something wrong about this allod...
Get ready then! Nobody knows what happens next...

Oh... Astral be praised!
Can you help me to disable the Pyramid? I don't need treasures anymore! I just want to get out of here...

Your visit to our land comes at a dire time...
We've renounced Armando, our creator, and fled to this island lost deep in the astral. The natives were decent folk, and we've been living peacefully side by side, exchanging their blood for our goods and knowledge. And curse be upon those shapeshifters for trying to destroy our alliance!
If you're willing to help us, you'll have to defeat the shapeshifters' chieftain named Luth the Meager, and he's as cruel and ruthless a bastard as I've met in all of my days.
But first you'll need to protect both villages from the shapeshifters! In the center of each village there's a security seal that can create a barrier that those shifters can't breach. All you need to do is activate the seal and hold out for a while.
I will help you by temporarily bestowing my dark gift upon you. Don't be afraid, you're not going to become a vampire. We have given a vow not to beget the likes of us any longer. However, the power of blood will help you in battle. As long as you're satiated and the blood runs hotly through your veins, you alone will be worth a good dozen in combat! But there's a catch, and that's the eternal thirst, a faint semblance of which you're about to experience.
If you feel hungry or exhausted, drink some fresh blood. Any human on this island will gladly let you have a sip. After all, you're our only hope! If there are no humans around, you can settle for the blood of an animal. It doesn't taste quite as good, but the thirst will be quenched... for a while!
Now go! All of us, both humans and vampires, are pinning our hopes on you.
Only, don't run ahead, mind! Fight fair! If outsiders run ahead, Capa gets angry!
Outsiders are cowardly, they are afraid to argue with Capa! Then off you go to meet your death, strangers. When you are killed, Capa will go on and will kill everyone himself and take the treasure!

You can see a Xadaganian helmet right on the frozen throne and you can hear its voice...
‘It is time,’ says the helmet.
For a second, it sounds like the voice comes from the ice.

This is an excellent opportunity to earn glory, honors, and respect, and to acquire unique equipment and other valuable items. There are two teams fighting in a Skirmish. The idea is to find out who's the best, who's the strongest. There are no friends or allies. An Imperial team may face another Imperial team, League may fight League.

There are several arenas, each giving you the Signs of Victory. Use these signs to obtain Battleground Emblems and trade them for various prizes!
Do you want to confront other heroes in a fair combat? Welcome to the Battleground!

There are two unequal teams in this battleground. The bastion is occupied by six strong defenders. Twenty four weaker players attack the bastion. Their goal is to break into the bastion and kill all the defenders or capture their flag to win. They have nine tries of 3 minutes each, and if they fail to stay within the time limits, the onslaught stops, the dead revive, the attackers return to the ship and prepare for the next onslaught. If they fail for 9 times, the bastion defenders win. Find out what tips the scale, the skill or the number!

There are two teams of twelve people in this Battleground. They fight for the flag on the hill. The flag cannot be captured, but you will receive victory points for every team member near it. However, there’s no use flocking around the flag: there are two cannons on either side of the hill, capable of turning any player into thin spread. Whoever is the first to hit the victory score, wins the battleground.

There are two teams of twelve people in this Battleground. The main goal is to capture and hold control points: the mill, the lumber mill and Zem ruins. To capture, tap on a flag near a location and prevent enemies from tapping it. While you are holding a flag, your team will be scoring victory points. Hold more flags to collect points faster. Whoever is the first to hit the victory score, wins the battleground.

Hello there! How can I help you?

Helping your friends is good! Any creature may attack them, and who's going to be there to protect them, but you? You may give a hand not only to your best friends, but to anybody you choose to, provided that you are going to Astral allods. Meet me in the hangar, if you're interested.

Normally two heroes with a significant difference in levels cannot go down to the same dungeon or Astral Isle. This rule does not affect best friends. However, the stronger best friend is not able to just smash the enemy. Instead, they cover their best friend's back and support them. The little one thus obtains five new abilities: one increases damage, another protects from enemies' spells, the third one heals, the fourth one casts fear on the enemy, and the last one teleports the party to the dungeon entrance, just like Mage's Sanctuary. Best friends can invite other heroes to their party, but the stronger best friend's abilities do not apply to them.

If you want to help your best friend, just tell me, I will cast a Helping Hand on you. While it lasts, you may visit Astral Isles together with your best friend, and not spend any keys. You won't get any loot, either. Tell me as soon as you're done.
Once a half an hour you may teleport to each other, provided that you both are not in combat. When you're done, you may teleport back to your initial location.

Who may you safely lend your Astral ship? Why, your best friend, of course! Enter the hangar together, summon your ship and lend it to your best friend. The things they can do to the ship are the same as you can do: summon, undock from hangars, travel to Astral isles, enter battles, take damage and repair it. One thing they are unable to perform, is changing your ship's devices.
You cannot summon your ship while your best friend is holding it. To get it back, you have to enter the hangar together once again and ask for it. The ship will automatically return to you once your friendship is over.
Bear in mind, that all cargo on the ship will disappear as soon as your best friend gets hold of your ship!

A best friend is so near and dear that you could easily trust them with your life or light-heartedly lend them your mount. It is as easy as one, two, three! Enter your stable, choose a mount you would like to lend and share it! If your best friend has an empty slot, the mount you have chosen will gallop right into it, and all their Incarnations will be able to ride it as well! It's just as easy to return it, you only need to open the stable.
There are, however, two restrictions. First, a mount whose rank is 5 or higher is faithful to you, so make sure to share only mounts of ranks 1 to 4. Second, color patterns belong to you and cannot be shared.

By fulfilling my tasks, you will learn more about the area, see its beauty, and help the inhabitants of this region. Once you complete all my tasks, you will be given a valuable reward.
However, lately we've been getting complaints that our tasks are not easy to complete. Well, we are willing to assist you. You can buy symbols of this area and valuable resources from me - that will complete two of my tasks and financially support the Institute of Local History.

Done! Now you can freely use Nezebgrad portals! But at first you'll have to report to every Keeper. Inform them that you are allowed to use the portals.

What? You?!

No, it has nothing to do with you. We are looking for a descendant of the Legendary Orc who could wield one of the types of higher magic - elemental, necromancy, and so forth...
Oh please, you are no psionicist. You're just a weird shaman.
That's right, put these strange ideas out of your head and focus on finding the real descendant of the Legendary Orc.

We're working on more than ten major projects at the ZIT. And what does the City Council do? Take away my best employees for their horrible experiments! How can they expect us to finish our work on time?
I hope you didn't think I would just hand the piece of paper over to you.

We're working on more than ten major projects at the ZIT. And what does the City Council do? Take away my best employees for their horrible experiments! How can they expect us to finish our work on time?
Here, take this one and don't lose it!
Ha ha, very funny. Everyone knows there are no orc psionicists. You're just a weird shaman, my friend!
Listen, I have no time for this tomfoolery, my hands are full as it is. Go play your tricks in the Old Square.
Are you trying to tell me something, child?
Don't even think about it. These are special prisoners. I was ordered by the City Council to guard them personally.
Well? Why are you staring at me?
What? No, you are destined to find the descendant of the Legendary Orc, and that's it.
What? No, you are destined to find the descendant of the Legendary Orc, and that's it.
Ahaha! What are you babbling... There are no orc psionicists! Or rather, we have yet to find them. But you're definitely not one of them. You're just a weird shaman!

I'm only a guardsman. Who might want to save someone like me? No one is going to save us. It's all a big joke.
When I was a child, I dreamt of becoming a general, but they told me only children of generals would be allowed to reach that rank. So I ended up becoming a cannoneer. Boom! Hah! I even have a marksmanship badge. Do you want to see it? Hm, where is it? It's gone! Did you steal it?
They'll come after you eventually! Who? They... They'll be here soon. The Empire will be finished, and I'll be a general. That's how it's going to be!

This is humiliating! A delicate woman like me in the arms of Imperial dogs! I remember how I used to dream of being captured. They would chain me up, undress me... It seemed so exciting! But this isn't like that at all. It's cold and the food is awful.
But I know that the League Army won't leave me here. My family will make them do something! ...At least that priest was kind to me. Oh Ignat, you are so wonderful!
It is not that easy! You cannot walk or ride there. I will teach you a spell, which will teleport you directly to the Kingdom of Nature at any moment you like.
Believe what? If you're having... some kind of issue, you should go to the medical unit, it's to the south of here.

Uh... Hang on... wait here. I'm going to call the doctor.

Just stay calm. They can fix you!

All right. Just don't get anxious. It happens!

It's stress and hot weather - it's cooking your brain, hah.

You gotta understand - there are no orc psionicists... And you... you're just a weird shaman.

Just keep your mouth shut, or you'll get hauled off to a mental hospital one of these days.
Done! Now you can use this portal!

The ogres are very dangerous. It won't be easy to lure them into a trap. For bait you should use the meat of wild boars. They live all over this allod so they should be easy to find.
After you gather a lot of meat you should throw it into a cage. The ogres should eventually be unable to resist the food and enter the trap.

This body is pretty weak and skeleton-like. Couldn't you do any better than this?! Oh well. I'm going to get drunk and pick up a few female Chosen Ones. Hopefully one day I'll learn to look at my reflection without disgust.

Hah! What do you expect me to do? I don't care if they chose a cherry tree as their leader! Let them worship a tea cup or dragon droppings! I don't give a damn!
Sorry but I can't turn into a ghost again. The mere thought of it makes my stomach turn. Surely there must be another way to find out this name.

What do you expect will come of this? It's not a big deal to spend half the day in the bushes. We're quite used to that. You just have to find a place with a lot of leaves.
As for my liver, I'll just jump off the allod. Death can cure illnesses, you know. The higher you jump, the quicker suffering ends!

That'll be easy! What a brilliant idea! We can't do anything to him until we combine our souls, and then I'll be able to drag all the names out of him. I'll be able to find out the names of all his cousins if I want!
Now, why are you looking at me like that? Are you up to something? You're not planning to lure me out so he can possess my body, do you? Not bloody likely, good sir. I'm not a simpleton!

What? The cultist was castrated? Turn around, let me check... Oh, bloody hell! What a terrible joke that was! Although, he is a pretty worthless loser. It probably wouldn't make much of a difference. If I were him, I'd probably join a cult as well... A cult of girls!
I'm not going to be a part of this! Damn everything! Change everything back the way it was! I'd rather be a ghost of a hero than a live as the village clown...

Helping your friends is good! Any creature may attack them, and who's going to be there to protect them, but you? You may give a hand not only to your best friends, but to anybody you choose to, provided that you are going to Astral allods. Meet me in the hangar, if you're interested.

Normally two heroes with a significant difference in levels cannot go down to the same dungeon or Astral Isle. This rule does not affect best friends. However, the stronger best friend is not able to just smash the enemy. Instead, they cover their best friend's back and support them. The little one thus obtains five new abilities: one increases damage, another protects from enemies' spells, the third one heals, the fourth one casts fear on the enemy, and the last one teleports the party to the dungeon entrance, just like Mage's Sanctuary. Best friends can invite other heroes to their party, but the stronger best friend's abilities do not apply to them.

If you want to help your best friend, just tell me, I will cast a Helping Hand on you. While it lasts, you may visit Astral Isles together with your best friend, and not spend any keys. You won't get any loot, either. Tell me as soon as you're done.
Once a half an hour you may teleport to each other, provided that you both are not in combat. When you're done, you may teleport back to your initial location.

Who may you safely lend your Astral ship? Why, your best friend, of course! Enter the hangar together, summon your ship and lend it to your best friend. The things they can do to the ship are the same as you can do: summon, undock from hangars, travel to Astral isles, enter battles, take damage and repair it. One thing they are unable to perform, is changing your ship's devices.
You cannot summon your ship while your best friend is holding it. To get it back, you have to enter the hangar together once again and ask for it. The ship will automatically return to you once your friendship is over.
Bear in mind, that all cargo on the ship will disappear as soon as your best friend gets hold of your ship!

"Never give your love away," the Kanians say. Why, but of course you can trust a best friend with your mount! Enter your stable, choose a mount you would like to lend and share it! If your best friend has an empty slot, the mount you have chosen will gallop right into it, and all their Incarnations will be able to ride it as well! It's just as easy to return it, you only need to open the stable.
There are, however, two restrictions. First, a mount whose rank is 5 or higher is faithful to you, so make sure to share only mounts of ranks 1 to 4. Second, color patterns belong to you and cannot be shared.
Excellent! Now you can fly around as much as you want. You won't spend any keys. You won't get any loot at the Isle, either. But you don't charge for helping a friend, eh!
We are experienced astralonauts! We used to shoot these cannons at Octulhu! If you don't want any loot, you may just go and help your friends there. Good luck to you out there, in the Astral!
Enough is enough. Ah well, one cannot sponge off their friends forever! Now you will be spending your keys and receive loot again!
